## What's the Minimum Wage in Australia? A Complete Guide to Hourly to Annual Conversion

If you've ever asked yourself **what's the minimum wage in Australia**, you're not alone. Whether you're negotiating a salary, budgeting for a new job, or just checking your pay, understanding how your hourly rate translates to annual income is essential. This guide covers the National Minimum Wage, award rates, casual loading, superannuation, and how tax and the Medicare levy affect your take-home pay.

### How to Convert Hourly Rate to Annual Salary

The standard formula is simple: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**. For full-time employees, we assume a 38-hour week (the standard under the Fair Work Act). So if you earn the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, your annual gross pay is:

$26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,252.64

This figure is before tax, Medicare, and any salary sacrifice arrangements. It also assumes you work the same hours every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. For part-time or casual workers, adjust the hours per week accordingly. The [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool on this site does the maths for you.

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage is set by the Fair Work Commission and applies to employees not covered by an award or agreement. From 1 July 2026, it is **$26.44 per hour**, or **$1,004.90 per week** for 38 hours. However, most workers are covered by industry or occupation awards that often pay higher rates. For example, the Hospitality Award or the General Retail Industry Award have minimum rates above the national minimum. If you're unsure, check your award on the Fair Work Ombudsman website or use the [pay guides](/blog) on this site.

**Important:** The National Minimum Wage is a floor, not a median. If you see an average figure like the ABS Average Weekly Earnings (May 2026: $2,083.70 per week for full-time adults), that is an average across all industries, not the median for your specific job. Always compare your rate to the relevant award or enterprise agreement.

### Casual Loading: What It Means for Your Pay

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave (annual leave, sick leave, etc.). For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is **$33.05 per hour** ($26.44 × 1.25). When using the [timesheet](/), you can check the 'casual loading' box to automatically add 25%. **Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading** – the calculator applies it correctly.

### Fortnightly Pay: A Handy Figure

Many Australians are paid fortnightly. To estimate your gross fortnightly pay, multiply your weekly pay by 2. For a full-time worker on the National Minimum Wage:

$1,004.90 per week × 2 = $2,009.80 per fortnight (before tax).

This can help with budgeting between pay cycles. The [reference tables](/data) on this site provide quick conversions for common hourly rates.

### Tax and Medicare Levy on Your Annual Salary

Once you have your annual gross figure, you can estimate tax using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income over $190,000

Plus, the Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. For the National Minimum Wage example ($52,252.64):

- Tax: $0 on first $18,200, then 15% on $26,800 ($4,020), then 30% on $7,252.64 ($2,175.79) = total tax $6,195.79
- Medicare levy: 2% of $52,252.64 = $1,045.05
- Total deductions: $7,240.84
- Estimated take-home pay: $45,011.80 per year, or about $865.61 per week.

Note: The Medicare levy reduction thresholds for 2026–27 were not confirmed in this estimate, so we use the 2025–26 single thresholds. This estimate does not include the Medicare levy surcharge, HELP repayments, or salary packaging.

### Superannuation: Paid on Top

From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee is **12%** of your ordinary earnings, paid by your employer on top of your salary. It does not reduce your take-home pay. For the National Minimum Wage annual salary of $52,252.64, your employer would contribute an extra $6,270.32 in super, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Super is not included in the annual pay figure shown on this site – it's a separate benefit. Learn more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

### Putting It All Together

Whether you're checking **what's the minimum wage in Australia** or converting a higher hourly rate, the process is the same. Use the [timesheet](/) on this site to enter your base hourly rate, add casual loading if applicable, and see your annual, monthly, fortnightly, and weekly figures. The calculator also estimates tax and Medicare based on the 2026–27 rates.

Remember: The figures here are estimates. Your actual pay may differ due to award rates, enterprise agreements, unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. Always consult your employer or the Fair Work Ombudsman for your specific situation.

### Disclaimer

Annual pay shown here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
